newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end off, Florida awaits coldest night.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end off, Florida awaits coldest night.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended slightly weaker as the market awaited Florida's coldest weather this winter but no damage was expected to the remaining crop, traders and forecasters said.
March orange juice rose to pierce the 18-day moving average, but suffered a technical retreat to below the four-day moving average, traders noted.
"We are sitting below this 80.00 cent level and I think technically we are going to come down further," a trader said.
March orange juice settled 0.50 cent weaker at 79.90 cents per pound, traded 81.50 to 79.75 cents. Volume was estimated at 2,500 lots.

"This will be the coldest night of the winter season down there, but probably not cold enough to do any damage," David Taylor of Weather Services Corp said. "They are also well ahead in harvesting the fruit."
Temperatures would have to plunge to 25 degrees Fahrenheit to cause damage but temperatures were likely to bottom around 30 to 35 degrees, causing frost in some spots, Taylor said.
